assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock, built on Katori's magic-wavelength proposal and developed to 10^-18 fractional uncertainty, is a clear and original measurement advance. It redefines the limits of timekeeping, enables searches for variation of constants and dark-sector physics, and underlies relativistic geodesy.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed and first realised the magic-wavelength lattice concept; Ye's group drove the strontium clocks to the best uncertainties and the clock-comparison and many-body physics. Two laureates give a clean configuration. Ye's overlap with the earlier frequency-comb prize is a presentational matter, not a bar. Other contributors (e.g. Lemonde, Takamoto) are not in the credited names.
assessment.maturity: Independent confirmation across several laboratories and species (Sr, Yb) is strong, and the interpretation is stable. A redefinition of the second is under discussion, so recognition is timely and not premature.
uncertainties: Whether the committee judges the atomic-clock theme already honoured by the 2005 and 1989 prizes.
Relative weight of Katori's proposal versus the experimental precision race is a judgment call.
I rely on my own background knowledge of the history and have not verified details.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum simulation with ultracold atoms in optical lattices gives controllable, clean realisations of Hubbard-type many-body models, such as the superfluid-Mott transition, Fermi-Hubbard antiferromagnetism and many-body localisation. It connects directly to statistical mechanics of interacting systems and is a lasting methodological shift.
assessment.attribution: The credited set has five names. Zoller (with Jaksch, Cirac) supplied the theoretical proposals, and Bloch and Greiner the experimental realisations including the microscope. Esslinger and Cirac are also strong, so any three-person selection leaves out decisive contributors. My choice balances theory with the two most identified experimentalists.
assessment.maturity: Well replicated across many groups for over two decades, but the headline goal of solving open problems such as the Fermi-Hubbard phase diagram is still partly open. This is mature as a technique and ongoing as a science.
uncertainties: Credit allocation among five strong contributors is genuinely unresolved.
Overlap with the 2001 and 2012 AMO prizes and with the trapped-ion and Rydberg candidates.
Whether the field's scientific payoff beyond demonstration is judged sufficient.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene opened moiré flat-band physics, with correlated insulators and superconductivity in a tunable carbon system. The Bistritzer-MacDonald flat-band prediction and its experimental realisation form a rare theory-experiment pair that created a major new field.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the decisive prediction of the magic angle; Jarillo-Herrero's group delivered the experimental discovery, but the list's names omit Yuan Cao as first author and others, which complicates the attribution. The three-name set is plausible but not obviously complete.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced by many groups and extended to other moiré systems, but the mechanism of the superconductivity and correlated states is still debated, so recognition may be somewhat early.
uncertainties: Origin of the superconductivity and the strongly correlated phases remains disputed.
Possible roles of other contributors (e.g. Kim, Dean, Young) who are not listed.
Whether eight years is a long enough horizon for the committee.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The cavity method and survey propagation applied to random constraint-satisfaction problems exposed the clustering and condensation (glassy) structure of the solution space. This transferred spin-glass replica ideas to computation, inference and learning, with broad impact in complex-systems theory.
assessment.attribution: Mézard and Zecchina, with Parisi, developed the cavity approach and the survey-propagation algorithm for random K-SAT. Parisi's role is recognised by the 2021 prize, which makes this a natural complement, and the two credited names are a fair, compact pair.
assessment.maturity: The theory is mathematically supported in parts (e.g. rigorous results on satisfiability thresholds) and widely used in statistical inference and coding. Experimental confirmation is not the right criterion, but the impact on computer science has been mixed, so it may still be viewed as a follow-on to 2021.
uncertainties: Overlap with Parisi's 2021 recognition could weigh against a second spin-glass-related award.
Predictions are partly non-rigorous; some replica-symmetry-breaking statements rest on physical arguments.
Practical algorithmic impact versus conceptual impact is uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Higgs boson discovery at the LHC confirmed the mechanism of electroweak symmetry breaking and completed the Standard Model, so its importance is beyond question. Recognising the conception and construction of ATLAS and CMS would honour an unusually large collaborative achievement.
assessment.attribution: The 2013 prize recognised the theory. The experimental credit is spread over thousands of people, and the three listed names are founders and spokespersons of ATLAS and CMS, but not the only decisive contributors; an individual-based attribution is hard to defend fully and the statutes constrain the allocation.
assessment.maturity: The discovery is fully confirmed with a large body of coupling measurements, and recognition is long-awaited. Maturity is not a concern; fair attribution is.
uncertainties: Whether the committee accepts instrument-building leadership as a basis for individual laureates.
Omission of other key figures, such as accelerator and detector pioneers, is likely to be contested.
I cannot verify the ranking of individual contributions from the supplied text.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Time-reversal-invariant topological insulators and the quantum spin Hall effect established a new class of quantum matter with protected edge and surface states, with the theory-experiment link (HgTe) being clear. It built directly on the topological-matter concepts recognised in 2016.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele predicted the Z2 quantum spin Hall state; Molenkamp's group realised it in HgTe wells (with Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang giving the HgTe prediction, who are not credited here), and Hasan's group demonstrated 3D topological insulators. Four names are credited, so a three-person selection leaves Hasan out, which will be contentious. Zhang's death also limits the configuration.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed across many materials and techniques, though technological applications are not yet realised. The concept is widely accepted and stable.
uncertainties: Missing credited contributors (Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang) in the underlying HgTe prediction.
Whether the committee sees this as too close to 2016.
Choice between Hasan and Mele for the third position is uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The KTHNY theory of defect-mediated two-dimensional melting predicted a hexatic phase with power-law orientational order, extending topological-defect ideas into the statistical physics of soft and condensed matter. It is conceptually elegant and has lasting influence on the physics of defects and phase transitions.
assessment.attribution: Halperin and Nelson developed the dislocation-unbinding theory and the hexatic phase, and Young contributed to the theory and the numerical elucidation. Kosterlitz and Thouless were recognised in 2016, so this is the unrecognised complement; attribution is reasonably well defined but could be argued to include only Halperin and Nelson.
assessment.maturity: Experimental confirmation in colloids, liquid crystals and simulations was gradual and in part disputed (first or second order melting depending on the system). The idea is solid, but the recognition is late and the 2016 prize already covered the key concept.
uncertainties: Whether the 2016 prize already captured the essential discovery.
Whether Young's contribution is comparable to Halperin's and Nelson's.
Details of melting scenario in specific systems remain unsettled.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The discovery that cells organise their interior by liquid-liquid phase separation into condensates, together with an active-droplet physical theory, links soft-matter and statistical physics to cell biology. It is a major new view of intracellular organisation, close to my interest in interdisciplinary stochastic and active systems.
assessment.attribution: Brangwynne and Hyman made the experimental discovery with P granules; Jülicher supplied physical theory of active droplets. A fair configuration is plausible, though many biologists and theorists (e.g. Rosen, Pappu, Parker) also contributed, so the allocation is unsettled.
assessment.maturity: The paradigm is widely adopted, but the biological significance of phase separation versus other assembly mechanisms is still debated, and the physical theory is not yet quantitatively validated in vivo. It may be premature as a physics prize and could fit biology better.
uncertainties: Whether the work falls within the remit of the physics prize.
Controversy about whether many reported condensates are true liquid phases.
Credit allocation between experimental and theoretical contributors.
